results.title: Saudi Arabia braces for thunderstorms, flash floods across most regions through Tuesday

results.title: Hanon Systems Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
results.description: Revenue reached KRW 2.66 trillion, with operating profit of KRW 120.6 billion; cumulative operating profit increased 77.9% year-on-year Operating margin reached 4.5%, supported by enhanced operational efficiency and continued cost-improvement initiatives Electrification increased to 33% of total revenue while the company continues to strengthen the foundation for mid- to long-term growth SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hanon Systems, a leading global automotive thermal management supplier and a subsidiary of Hankook & Company Group, today announced its financial results for the third quarter of 2026. The company reported consolidated revenue of KRW 2.66 trillion and an operating profit of KRW 120.6 billion. Although revenue declined slightly by 1.8% year-on-year, reflecting temporary volume adjustments by customers and exchange fluctuations, operating profit increased by 26.6% year-on-year and 16.3% quarter-on-quarter, bringing the operating margin to 4.5%. For the first nine months of the year, cumulative revenue reached KRW 8.2804 trillion, up 1.2% year-on-year, while cumulative operating profit increased 77.9% to KRW 321.5 billion, demonstrating a significant improvement in profitability. Hanon Systems' continued efforts to strengthen cost competitiveness through operational efficiency are delivering tangible results, despite ongoing demand volatility in the global automotive market. In the third quarter, the cost of goods sold (COGS) ratio improved by 0.6 percentage points, declining from 89.1% to 88.5%. The selling, general, and administrative (SG&A) expense ratio also decreased from 7.3% to 7.0%. For the first nine months of the year, the cumulative COGS ratio improved by 2.0 percentage points, decreasing from 91.1% to 89.1%, reflecting the positive impact of company-wide efforts to enhance operational efficiency. Although sales in Europe increased, consolidated revenue declined by 1.8% year-on-year, primarily due to a lower sales volume resulting from production disruptions at a major domestic customer. Meanwhile, the share of revenue from electrification increased from 31% in the second quarter to 33% in the third quarter. The company will continue to strengthen its business competitiveness by addressing evolving global market demands and leveraging its comprehensive portfolio of thermal management solutions. Hanon Systems is also pursuing business diversification, leveraging the technical expertise and global operational capabilities developed through its core automotive thermal management business. The company is advancing its aftermarket business, with a full market launch planned by 2026. It has already initiated product sales in the domestic market through "T-Station" and is accelerating the expansion of global sales channels. A key milestone in this effort was securing an initial order from Inter Cars, a leading automotive parts distributor in Europe. In addition, the company is exploring opportunities to extend its thermal management technologies into the off-road mobility sector, including agricultural machinery, construction equipment, and defense systems. In addition to its core automotive business, Hanon Systems is also expanding its technology portfolio to secure new growth opportunities in other industries. Building on its established thermal management expertise, the company has begun developing solutions for energy storage systems (ESS), power conversion systems (PCS), and solid-state transformers (SST). At the same time, the company is taking a phased approach to entering the thermal management market for AI data center servers, while actively identifying business opportunities to establish a foundation for mid- to long-term growth. Vice Chairman and CEO Soo Il Lee stated, "Despite ongoing uncertainties in the global market, our continued focus on fundamental process improvements and operational efficiency has enabled us to maintain stable business performance." He added, "Going forward, we will continue to respond to changes in the electrification market, identify new growth opportunities that leverage our thermal management expertise, and further strengthen the foundation for sustainable growth." Q3 2026 Q3 2025 Q2 2026 Revenue KRW 2.6569 trillion KRW 2.7057 trillion KRW 2.8752 trillion Operating Profit KRW 120.6 billion KRW 95.3 billion KRW 103.7 billion About Hanon Systems Hanon Systems, founded in 1986, is a global leader in thermal management solutions. In January 2025, it became a subsidiary of Hankook & Company Group. Its offering includes a wide range of solutions in the areas of heating, ventilation and air conditioning, powertrain cooling, compressor, fluid transport, and electronics and fluid pressure. The company currently operates 50 manufacturing sites and three regional innovation centers and employs more than 20,000 people across 21 countries. To learn more, visit hanonsystems.com. results.title: FORMER SGX CIO & CTO TINKU GUPTA APPOINTED VICE CHAIRMAN OF WISSEN TECHNOLOGY SINGAPORE
results.description: Appointment strengthens Wissen's Singapore leadership and growth ambitions, building on its expanding client relationships and engineering-led technology capabilities. SINGAPORE, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Wissen Technology, a global technology services and solutions company, is strengthening its Singapore presence through a delivery-led approach built on deep engineering expertise, a product-engineering mindset and a focus on solving complex business problems. Building on early client wins with strategic clients, the company has appointed Tinku Gupta, former CIO and CTO of SGX Group, as Vice Chairman of Wissen Technology Singapore, strengthening its leadership as it expands its regional ambitions. Tinku Gupta, Vice Chairman of Wissen Technology Singapore Wissen's approach centres on combining engineering excellence with business understanding to help enterprises modernise critical technology platforms, accelerate innovation and deliver measurable outcomes. Its growing client base in Singapore reflects the relevance of this approach across businesses seeking reliable, scalable and future-ready technology solutions. Ms. Gupta brings more than 30 years of experience across technology, financial market infrastructure, business operations and cybersecurity. During her career at SGX, she held leadership roles across business, technology, and operations – most recently serving as CIO and CTO. In her technology roles, she oversaw major modernisation initiatives while sustaining the resilience of mission-critical trading and clearing infrastructure. Earlier, as Business Head of Market Data & Access, she was responsible for growing the business through the development and launch of strategic products and services. Commenting on the appointment, Raghu Pareddy, Founder & CEO, Wissen Technology, said, "At Wissen, we believe strong engineering must begin with a clear understanding of the business problem and the outcomes that matter to the client. Our growing presence in Singapore, including early engagements with leading enterprises across financial services and other sectors, reflects the confidence clients place in our engineering and delivery capabilities." "As Vice Chairman, Tinku will support Wissen Technology Singapore's growth and client engagement strategy. She brings an important additional dimension to our leadership - technology expertise combined with the perspective of having led major delivery initiatives within a leading financial market infrastructure institution. Her experience will help us strengthen the connection between what clients need and what we engineer and deliver, as we build our next phase of growth in Singapore." adds Raghu Ms. Tinku Gupta, Vice Chairman, Wissen Technology Singapore, said, "Having spent much of my career on the enterprise side, I understand that technology decisions are ultimately judged by the business outcomes they deliver. Engineering excellence is essential, but it must go hand in hand with an understanding of the client's priorities, operating realities and long-term ambitions. Wissen's product-engineering mindset and delivery-led approach resonate strongly with this belief. I look forward to bringing that perspective to the team, strengthening our client relationships and contributing to Wissen's continued growth in Singapore." Tinku Gupta holds a Master's degree in Electronics and Telecommunications Engineering with First Class Honours and has completed the AI Senior Executive programme at the National University of Singapore and a Professional Certificate in Coaching from Singapore Management University. About Wissen Technology Wissen Technology is a global technology services and solutions provider that combines strategy, design and engineering to help enterprises achieve digital transformation at scale. Founded in the United States in 2000, the company has expanded its global footprint across India, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, the UAE, Singapore and Canada. With more than two decades of expertise, Wissen has delivered over US$1 billion worth of projects and serves more than 20 Fortune 500 companies across banking and financial services, telecom, healthcare, retail, manufacturing and energy. For more information, visit https://www.wissen.com/ for further updates, visit LinkedIn profile: https://in.linkedin.com/company/wissen-technology

results.title: Israel faces new era of sinking US support after election
results.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's brash campaign posters are still up on Israeli public buses -- images of him, US President Donald Trump and soaring warjets that laud the two leaders attacking Iran together. Neither is now advertising the state of the two countries' alliance. A week after an inconclusive election for Netanyahu, Americans overwhelmingly rejected Trump and chose a Congress led by Democrats who want a tougher approach to Israel, whether on Iran, Gaza or settler violence in the occupied West Bank.

results.title: Global solidarity delivers major boost to Education Cannot Wait as "Hope Starts Here" campaign approaches its US$600 million goal
results.description: Governments announce US$ 405.8 million in new pledges at Geneva replenishment conference, bringing ECW to 90% of its funding target and opening new pathways for innovative partnerships to support education for crisis-affected children. GENEVA, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Governments and partners rallied behind the world's most vulnerable children today, announcing US$405.8 million in new pledges to Education Cannot Wait (ECW) at its High-Level Replenishment Conference, hosted by Switzerland in Geneva. Together with US$135.8 million in financial resources already secured through previous multi-year donor commitments, these pledges bring ECW's Hope Starts Here campaign total to US$541.6 million, reaching 90% of its US$600 million target. Participants gather at Education Cannot Wait’s High-Level Replenishment Conference in Geneva, Switzerland, on 5 November 2026, marking US$541.6 million in total pledges towards its US$600 million funding target to reach 10 million crisis-affected children with quality education. ECW expressed its deep gratitude to all governments and partners that stepped forward with financial commitments, reaffirming their solidarity with children affected by conflict, displacement and climate-related disasters at a time of growing humanitarian needs and shrinking international aid budgets. Germany, the United Kingdom, Norway, Canada, Switzerland, Ireland, EU, and Japan were among the governments whose commitments demonstrated continued international leadership and confidence in ECW's mission. Their collective support sends a powerful message: even in difficult times, the world cannot afford to turn its back on children's education. The conference marked a defining moment in ECW's tenth anniversary year, renewing the commitment made when the Fund was established in 2016: that children living through crises must not be left behind. Sigrid Kaag, Chair of ECW's High-Level Steering Group, said: "Education is a fundamental human right, even in times of conflict, displacement and disaster. Today's commitments are a powerful demonstration of international solidarity and a renewal of the promise we made ten years ago: that children caught in crises will not be left behind. That promise must now be translated into action." Switzerland's leadership in hosting the conference reinforced the importance of collective responsibility and sustained international cooperation to protect children's right to education. Ambassador Dominik Stillhart, Co-Chair of ECW's Executive Committee, said: "For more than a century, Geneva has been where the world comes together to address its toughest challenges, and one lesson stands out: education cannot be treated as an exception when crises strike. That is why Switzerland hosted this conference and pledged CHF 35 million to Education Cannot Wait for 2027 to 2030. But no country can do this alone. We need governments and partners to step up. Today, our partners chose to keep that promise funded." Since its establishment, ECW and its partners have reached more than 16 million children in crisis-affected countries. Yet the scale of the challenge continues to grow, with an estimated 258 million school-aged children and adolescents affected by crises worldwide. The commitments announced in Geneva provide a strong foundation for ECW's 2027–2030 Strategic Plan, which aims to reach 10 million children, half of them girls and including one million children with disabilities. The new strategy will strengthen ECW's ability to respond rapidly to emergencies while providing more sustained support in protracted crises, investing in quality learning, protection, inclusion and the resilience of national education systems. The conference also signalled growing momentum to explore new approaches to financing education in emergencies. Partnership offers and initiatives involving Porticus, the International Finance Facility for Education (IFFEd), the Education Bridging Fund (EBF) and Swiss cantonal banks highlighted opportunities to complement traditional donor contributions by mobilizing development finance and private capital. Discussions involving Enosis Capital, BNP Paribas and MetLife Investment Management also explored the potential of an education continuity outcome bond, currently under development, to mobilize investment for children affected by crises. These initiatives, at different stages of development and subject to further design and institutional approvals, could help ECW diversify its financing base and unlock additional resources in the years ahead. Beyond financing, high-level discussions brought together governments and partners from crisis-affected countries to demonstrate the importance of national leadership, including the integration of refugee and displaced children into national education systems and the need for more predictable financing that connects humanitarian response with longer-term recovery. For ECW, the Geneva conference represents a major milestone, but not the conclusion of the Hope Starts Here campaign. Building on the confidence and commitments demonstrated by partners, the Fund will now focus on translating this momentum into results for children. Maysa Jalbout, Director of Education Cannot Wait, said: "Today, our partners have given us more than financial commitments. They have placed their confidence in ECW and entrusted us with an enormous responsibility. We are deeply grateful. But the true measure of today's success will not be how much we have raised. It will be the difference we make in children's lives. Our work starts now." Looking ahead, ECW will focus on three priorities at the heart of its next strategic period. First, ensuring that children are learning. Access to education remains essential, but it is not enough. ECW will place greater emphasis on quality learning, alongside children's safety, mental health and well-being, ensuring that investments deliver meaningful and measurable results. Second, strengthening national and local leadership. ECW will work to bring decisions and resources closer to communities affected by crises, advancing its ambition to channel at least 50% of programme financing through national and local partners by 2030. Third, broadening the coalition that finances education in emergencies. Government contributions will remain the backbone of ECW's work, complemented by stronger partnerships with philanthropy, businesses, development banks and investors to mobilize additional and more predictable financing. With the replenishment target now within reach, ECW will continue engaging existing and prospective partners to close the remaining funding gap and build on the momentum generated in Geneva. Ten years after its creation, ECW enters its next chapter with renewed confidence, an ambitious strategy and a strengthened coalition of partners united by a common commitment: no child should have to wait for a crisis to end before they can learn. Notes to Editors About Education Cannot Wait: Education Cannot Wait (ECW) is the global fund for education in crises. The Fund provides rapid, flexible funding to locally-led education responses that protect learning for refugee, internally displaced and other children, while strengthening systems to sustain learning and resilience in fragile and conflict-affected contexts. ECW works with governments, public and private funders, UN agencies, civil society organisations, and other humanitarian and development aid actors so that no child is left behind. As global crises intensify and the education financing gap widens, ECW calls on public and private sector partners to scale up investments so millions more crisis-affected girls and boys can learn and rebuild their futures. Additional information available at: www.educationcannotwait.org For press inquiries: Rafik Elouerchefani: ecwcomms@un-ecw.org

results.title: A veteran Arab lawmaker in Israel is willing to break with precedent to topple Netanyahu
results.description: Ahmad Tibi, a prominent Arab lawmaker in Israel, is ready to form alliances with Jewish parties to challenge Prime Minister Netanyahu’s tenure. This move is unconventional and could face political challenges from both sides.

results.title: البرلمان التركي يقر «اتفاق مكة» للدفاع المشترك مع السعودية وباكستان
results.description: أقر البرلمان التركي، الخميس، مشروع قانون التصديق على «اتفاق مكة للدفاع المشترك» بين السعودية وتركيا وباكستان، في خطوة جديدة نحو استكمال الإجراءات القانونية لتفعيل الاتفاق الذي وقّعه قادة الدول الثلاث في مكة المكرمة خلال أغسطس الماضي، بهدف تعزيز الردع المشترك وتطوير التعاون العسكري والدفاعي.وذكرت وكالة «الأناضول» التركية أن الجمعية العامة للبرلمان وافقت على مشروع القانون عقب مناقشة مواده والتصويت عليه، بعد أن كانت لجنة الشؤون الخارجية قد أقرته في 27 أكتوبر الماضي.ومن المقرر إحالة القانون إلى الرئيس التركي رجب طيب أردوغان للتوقيع عليه ونشره في الجريدة الرسمية، استكمالاً لإجراءات التصديق. أنقرة: الاتفاق لا يستهدف أي دولة وخلال مناقشات البرلمان، أكد النائب عن حزب «العدالة والتنمية» ضياء ألطون يلدز، أن الاتفاقية تستهدف تعزيز التعاون الأمني والاستقرار الإقليمي، ولا تستهدف أي دولة ثالثة.وشدد على أن الهدف الأساسي للاتفاق يتمثل في منع النزاعات وتعزيز قدرات الردع، وليس توسيع دائرة الصراعات في المنطقة. هجوم على دولة.. اعتداء على الجميع وكانت مكة المكرمة شهدت في 7 أغسطس الماضي توقيع الاتفاقية خلال قمة استضافها قصر الصفا، بمشاركة ولي العهد رئيس مجلس الوزراء الأمير محمد بن سلمان، والرئيس التركي رجب طيب أردوغان، ورئيس الوزراء الباكستاني محمد شهباز شريف.وينص الاتفاق على أن «أي هجوم مسلح على أي من الدول الثلاث هو هجوم على الجميع»، بما يعزز مفهوم الدفاع المشترك، ويرسخ التعاون العسكري والأمني بين الرياض وأنقرة وإسلام آباد.ويهدف الاتفاق إلى تعزيز الردع المشترك في مواجهة التهديدات، وتطوير مختلف أوجه التعاون الدفاعي، بما يسهم في دعم أمن الدول الثلاث واستقرار المنطقة. أمانة في السعودية لتعزيز التنسيق وفي إطار الخطوات التنفيذية للاتفاق، اتفقت الدول الثلاث خلال اجتماع عقد في إسطنبول في 31 أغسطس الماضي على إنشاء أمانة في السعودية لدعم العمل المشترك وتنسيق الجهود في إطار الاتفاقية.وتقرر أن يتولى رئاسة الأمانة في مرحلتها الأولى أمين عام من باكستان لمدة ثلاث سنوات، بما يوفر إطاراً مؤسسياً لمتابعة تنفيذ الاتفاق وتعزيز التنسيق بين الأطراف الثلاثة. صناعات عسكرية وإنتاج مشترك ويمتد التعاون المنصوص عليه في الاتفاق إلى تعزيز القدرات الدفاعية ورفع مستوى التنسيق والتكامل بين القوات المسلحة للدول الثلاث، من خلال التدريبات والأنشطة العسكرية المشتركة.كما يشمل تطوير التعاون في الصناعات الدفاعية والتقنيات العسكرية، وتوسيع مجالات الإنتاج المشترك، بما يدعم القدرات الدفاعية للدول الثلاث، ويعزز جاهزيتها لمواجهة التحديات الأمنية.
